# Your Role
As a Corporate Executive, you're part of the Company's office staff at this site. You'll handle the paperwork that keeps the site running: accounts, freight, correspondence and trading. It isn't glamorous, but nothing here works without it.
## Who you report to Your line manager is the [bold]Corporate Liaison[/bold]. They represent the Company at this site and they're your first point of contact for anything work-related, from a question about a task to a problem with a colleague.
Some sites also have a [bold]Division Manager[/bold], who runs the site as a whole. If one is posted here, the Liaison reports to them. You won't usually deal with the Division Manager directly unless you're asked to.
If the Liaison isn't available, the most senior Executive present takes charge of the office until they're back.
## Your grade Everyone at the Company holds a grade, which is printed on your ID card. Office staff work their way through four grades: - [bold]WYC1 Trainee[/bold]: your probationary period. Nobody expects you to know everything yet, so ask questions. - [bold]WYC2 Junior Executive[/bold]: you've passed probation and you're a full member of staff. - [bold]WYC3 Executive[/bold]: you're experienced enough to help train new starters. - [bold]WYC4 Senior Executive[/bold]: you're trusted to run the office when the Liaison is away.
Promotion comes with time in the role. Keep your work up to standard and it'll follow.
## Other teams on site You'll work alongside a few other Company teams. You don't need to know how they work, but it helps to know who they are: - [bold]Corporate Security[/bold] look after the site, its staff and its property. If they ask you to do something for your safety, do it. - [bold]Research[/bold] staff work in the Company's laboratories under the Lead Researcher. Their work is confidential, so please don't ask them about it. - [bold]Company counsel[/bold] handle legal matters. If anyone mentions a contract, a complaint or a lawyer, pass it on to the Liaison.
